matches.stipulation: EMWC North American Championship (vacant)

Curtis Hansen pulls Whitecross off, tosses him the title, and Whitecross is the new North American Champion.

matches.stipulation: Loser Leaves the EMWC; no countouts and no disqualifications; the winner goes on to the Showtime World Title match
matches.note: Watkins bites Creed's forehead, stomps his gloved hand and superplexes him through a table; Watkins buries Creed under the wreckage, sends him in a laundry cart down the loading ramp into a Mustang, and the fight goes through the parking lot and onto the roof of the Creed Army bus before Watkins carries Creed back into the arena. Creed kicks out of a flying bulldog, a superbomb and a top-rope finisher of Watkins's own; Watkins kicks out of Creed's Goodnight Farewell Amen; Creed wins with the Triangle Creedplex. The two embrace and Watkins signals that Creed deserves the belt.

matches.stipulation: Non-title; no countouts; no disqualifications
matches.note: An unsanctioned fight, with neither the EMWC World Title nor the IIWF World Title on the line and no referee for most of it: Kowalski suckerpunches Hansen with a microphone, brings a ladder, tables, a dumpster and a barricade section into play, and Hansen fights back across the arena and the souvenir stand. Roscoe Law referees briefly and is thrown into the dumpster. Chris Blue hits Hansen with a chair and Kowalski ends it with the Skull Pump, then hands Hansen the EMWC title; Hansen says next time there will be a referee and a winner. No winner is named.

notes: The EMWC broadcast of 6 April 1998 from the United Center in Chicago, a three-hour edition posted in eleven parts, with Jon Stegglet, Lori Dane and Todd Michaelson at the announce table, Ken Graham announcing, Jon Keeton interviewing, and guest commentators Jeff Jomers and Eddy Bass calling the tag title match. Thirteen matches are worked: two North American Title qualifiers (Tony Starks and Gabriel Whitecross advance, and Whitecross wins the vacant title), the Phalanx lose the World Tag Team Championship to the Fraternity Boys, Joe Reed defends the Television Title twice, Creed beats Mad Dog Watkins in a loser-leaves match for his Showtime shot, and Curtis Hansen and Steve Kowalski fight without a winner. Kevin Slater's return, Ronnie D's set-up by J.W. Hardin, Brody Thunder and Simon Lebec, and Chris Blue's hiring of Kowalski fill the segments between. The card announces Showtime at the FleetCenter in Boston with Howard Stern as guest commentator, and a Moxy Blue challenge to Ronnie D for the following week.

Cut a promo denying he is a boy scout, mocking Sam Hell, Sid Snow and Dave Bryant, and was superkicked from behind by Bryant.
Before the broadcast, charged the ring and laid out Sam Hell and Sid Snow with his superkick.
After his match, hurdled the barricade and superkicked Jammin' Alan James.
With Elena, came to the ring at Dave Bryant's side and was chased around it by Jammin' Alan James.
With Glory, came to the ring at Dave Bryant's side and tried to alert the referee to the interference.
Came to the ramp with Grey Phoenix during Brian Lau's outburst, mocked Lau, and invoked a stipulation in his contract to challenge Lau to a match at Blood, Sweat, and Tears.
Chris Blue announced Greyson's match with Lau for 9 August.
At Kuyler Greyson's side; read Greyson's letter to President Blue.
Introduced Kabuki Kid and, at Quinn Brown's request, went to the back.
Followed Ms. Miki out and watched the Kabuki Kid match from the press table.
Hit Tiger Claw with a chair while the referee was down, which gave Sinister a pin the referee later reversed.
Came back to ringside with a chair, was blocked by Casey James, smacked him, and left through the crowd.
By phone from Pittsburgh, answered Curtis Hansen and Scott Alexander's challenge to a cell match at Blood, Sweat, and Tears: the Fraternity Boys do not back down.
At the announce table through the card with Jon Stegglet and Todd Michaelson as color commentator.

Announced the card for Blood, Sweat, and Tears at Texas Stadium on 9 August, including the Greyson and Lau match, Sinister's defense against Paragon, the Snake Den against Spector and Porter, a four-team cell for the World Tag Team titles, and the World title main event.

matches.stipulation: Before the broadcast
matches.note: Reported by Jon Stegglet at the top of the show: the two fought to a double disqualification when Dave Bryant charged the ring and laid both men out with his superkick.

matches.stipulation: EMWC Junior Heavyweight Title Tournament, first round; one fall, fifteen-minute limit
matches.note: La Pulga Gigante is carried out on a throne and rubs his rear end after each armdrag; Mota answers with a dropkick, a somersault plancha, a missile dropkick and a Shooting Star Press that puts Pulga through a table. Mota cuts his arm on the steel steps, Pulga works it with a moonsault and La Magistral, and the two trade a Tiger Suplex, an Ocean Cyclone suplex, a hurricanrana over the top, a powerbomb on the barricade, an Asai moonsault into the crowd and a triple-jump plancha. Pulga survives Mota's Splash Mountain crucifix powerbomb and Mota wins with a Skytwist Press and a one-arm cover.

matches.stipulation: EMWC Junior Heavyweight Title Tournament, first round; one fall
matches.note: Bryant comes out with Glory and Elena. Cool, winner of the King of the Cruisers tournament, takes the early advantage with a hiptoss, armdrags and an atomic drop; Bryant answers with a shoulderblock, a powerbomb, a snap suplex and a figure-four leglock. Jammin' Alan James runs out chasing Glory, hits Bryant with brass knuckles and rolls him in; the referee sees nothing, and Cool hits an Asai moonsault and covers.

matches.stipulation: EMWC Junior Heavyweight Title Tournament, first round
matches.note: Spector takes the opening with a brain buster and a spinning heel kick but misses a tope onto the Spanish table; Matsuoko answers with a cross body plancha, a somersault leg drop, a running senton and a Frog Splash, and Spector grabs the ropes at two. Spector hits the Cherry Blossom Bomber, and the Snake Den interrupts the cover: Spector goes after Ronnie D, Lebec hits him with a chair, and Kevin Slater slides in and hits Matsuoko with Sweet Dreams before leaving. Spector crawls across Matsuoko and gets the three.

matches.stipulation: EMWC Junior Heavyweight Title Tournament, first round; one fall, fifteen-minute limit extended by five minutes
matches.note: Brown asks that the match be one on one and Ms. Miki is sent to the back. The two trade armdrags, chops, a Shooting Star Press, a Ligerbomb, a powerbomb, a hurricanrana, Northern Lights and a Tiger Driver; the bell rings at fifteen minutes, the referee gives them five more, and Brown reverses Kabuki's top-rope powerbomb into a Frankensteiner for the three. The two shake hands.

matches.stipulation: EMWC Television Title tournament final; one fall; for a new EMWC Television Champion
matches.note: Tiger Claw comes out with Brian Lau; Claw works with kicks and knees, Sinister with a powerbomb on the concrete and a German suplex over the top rope. The referee is hit by Claw's kneebrace and Paragon comes in with a chair and hits Claw; Paragon tosses Sinister on top of him and the referee counts three, but after Brian Lau's protest and Kuyler Greyson's interruption he reviews the video on a monitor and rules that the match will continue. Lau brings Casey James out; Paragon smacks James, Chris Myers distracts the referee from Claw's Tiger Stretch, and Kevin Slater slides in and hits the Wild Ride on Claw. Sinister pins him after Thunder-Struck and is handed the Television title.

matches.stipulation: Four Corners match, worked as a three-way after Casey James was attacked backstage
matches.note: Alexander, Myers and Lebec go in without James, who is fighting Bobby Taylor outside: Myers hits a snap suplex, a cyclone suplex and a piledriver, Alexander a somersault splash, and Lebec a low shoulder, a bite and a shot with an object from his trunks. Lebec scores a Blackball on Alexander, hooks the trunks and gets the three.

matches.stipulation: EMWC World Heavyweight Championship (Slater defending)
matches.note: Tony Starks interrupts the introductions to taunt Slater about his wife, and Slater proposes a cell match for the title at Blood, Sweat, and Tears. Slater and Reed open with a show of sportsmanship and trade a pescado, a high cross body, a cyclone suplex, a flying elbow and a Spicoli Driver; the Syndicate comes to ringside, Reed clotheslines the referee, and Starks hits Slater with the title belt. Reed pulls Starks off Slater, Taylor and Myers go after the Syndicate, and Reed hits the Kentucky Backsmasher for the three and the title.

notes: The EMWC broadcast of 15 July 1998 from the MCI Center in Washington, D.C., a two-hour edition posted in six parts, with Jon Stegglet, Todd Michaelson and Richard Blue at the announce table and Ken Graham announcing. Before the broadcast Sam Hell and "Suicide" Sid Snow fought to a double disqualification. Seven matches are worked: four first-round matches of the Junior Heavyweight Title Tournament (Derek Mota, Big Greggy Cool, Steve Spector and Quinn Brown advance), the final of the Television Title tournament, in which Sinister beats Tiger Claw after a chair shot by Paragon is reversed on review, a Four Corners match worked as a three-way that Simon Lebec wins, and the main event, in which Joe Reed beats Kevin Slater for the World Heavyweight Championship. Chris Blue announces the card for Blood, Sweat, and Tears at Texas Stadium on 9 August.

name: Blood, Sweat, and Tears

date.source: The card's own heading, in the lines at the head of part one: Blood, Sweat, & Tears, live from Texas Stadium, Irving, Texas, August 9, 1998.

appearances.note: At the announce table with Jon Stegglet and Todd Michaelson through the card, in a powder-blue tuxedo and crescent-moon sunglasses; Kevin Slater joins the table for the Myers match.
Helped to the back for an MRI on his injured knee after the semifinal.
Introduced by Jon Keeton to a huge pop as the first of three special enforcers for the grudge match, and began an interview on why he is in the EMWC and why this match.
Finished his interview, promising to make sure Ronnie D and Simon Lebec face Trey Porter and Steve Spector fair and square and then to settle his own business with them.
Introduced first of the three enforcers, already in the ring; when the match began he yanked Ronnie D off the apron and threw Simon Lebec back into the ring.

Pulled Simon Lebec down from the apron as Ronnie D charged, and Ronnie D hit the turnbuckle; after the match he was superkicked by Zack Malone, beaten by the Body Shop and, after a handshake, hit with a chair by Ken Curtis.
Shown backstage with the Television Title next to Lori Dane, who offers to wash the belt.
After the bell, beat Paragon with the title belt and, with his wife in his arms, told him he had earned it but that one day he would hunt for it again.
The announcers say Paragon had kidnapped and held her for a couple of months; she was absent at the start of the match, then shown in a cage lowered over the ring, and ran to Sinister once it opened.
Shown before his semifinal in a recorded interview, in Spanish with English subtitles, with his father; named Tiger Claw, Derek Mota and Quinn Brown as the men he had to beat.
After the final, thanked his father, Guadalajara, his family and the CLLL, breathed fire, and was told he would defend the title at the next An Evening To The Extreme.
Shown in the locker room rubbing his son's shoulders and leading him out before the semifinal; at ringside he shouted encouragement during the kataha jime.
Got into the ring and raised his son's arm after the win over Tiger Claw.
Pointed out at ringside by the announcers, who say he has trained his son all his life; supported his son after the final.
Came to the ring with Tiger Claw for the semifinal against Juvenil Infierno.
Came to the ring with Tiger Claw for the grudge match against Chris Myers.
Billed with Casey James for the match against Bobby Taylor.
Came to the ring with Tony Starks for the World title cell match and stood at ringside with Casey James and Hakiro Matsuoko.
Was floored by a right hand from Luke Steele when the Syndicate learned Steele was with the Cult of Personality.
In a backstage interview with Jon Keeton before the triple threat, said he did not care about winning and would knock Alan James and Dave Bryant to hell and back.
Took the microphone after the triple threat to challenge Dave Bryant to finish it one on one.

With Elena, walked Dave Bryant to the ring in a half-tee reading Property of Dave Bryant; Todd Michaelson left the booth to pinch her and she chased him around the ring; she helped take the chain out of Bryant's knee.
With Glory, walked Dave Bryant to the ring in a black silk dress; bared her chest on the apron to break a pin count and was pushed off the apron by Sam Hell.

In a recorded video on the roof of the EMWC building, beside an old wheelchair, listed the injuries that kept him out for ten months, said he had no doctor's clearance and that EMWC was cleared of liability, and dared Ronnie D to break his neck again.
After the grudge match, embraced Ronnie D, Simon Lebec and Zack Malone and told the crowd they were the Body Shop; mocked Steve Spector for trusting him.
Walked the Natural Predators to the ring for their match against Curtis Hansen and Chris Quigley.
Announced Texas Death Match rules before the first bell, adding no submission for Quigley.
Came out limping on a kneebrace with a sign mocking the Natural Predators, took a microphone as executive producer Charles Franks fumed, and called for his partner.
Stood in Kuyler Greyson's corner and traded punches with Casey James at ringside during the match between Brian Lau and Kuyler Greyson.
Stood in Kuyler Greyson's corner and was kicked by Tiger Claw outside the ring during the match between Brian Lau and Kuyler Greyson.
Stood at ringside with Casey James, climbed onto the apron to help Brian Lau during the match against Kuyler Greyson, and later rolled in to put Lau on the unconscious Greyson.
Disguised as the cell's cameraman, hit Kevin Slater with the camera, helped Tony Starks to his feet and hit Starks with a shin kick meant for Slater.
Stood at ringside with Tiger Claw and pulled Brian Lau under the ropes by the arm to break Kuyler Greyson's anklelock.
Came out during the Myers and Tiger Claw match and was met halfway down the aisle by Bobby Taylor, who fought him through the arena.
After beating Taylor, took the microphone, taunted Taylor's wife and young son at ringside, and dropped a lighter on the whiskey-soaked Taylor, setting him on fire; an attendant put the fire out.
Came to ringside with Hakiro Matsuoko to back Tony Starks in the cell.
Ran down to ringside with Tony Starks during the match between Brian Lau and Kuyler Greyson and was tackled by Quinn Brown.
Came to ringside with Casey James to back Tony Starks.
Ran down to ringside with Hakiro Matsuoko during the match between Brian Lau and Kuyler Greyson and was dropkicked by Kabuki Kid.

Came through the curtain during the Myers and Tiger Claw match and fought Kevin Slater up the aisle and into the crowd; Slater hit him with a Northern Lights Bomb in the ring afterward, until Brian Lau pulled him out.
Came out of the audience with Kabuki Kid during the match between Brian Lau and Kuyler Greyson and tackled Hakiro Matsuoko.
Came out of the audience with Quinn Brown, springboarded off the rail and dropkicked Tony Starks.
Ran down with Sho Satsuma and held back Tony Starks so Kabuki Kid could kick him.
Ran down with Agito Nakajima and hit Tiger Claw from behind.
Sat at ringside furious at the Syndicate, climbed into the ring with a chair meant for Brian Lau and hit Kuyler Greyson instead when Lau pulled him into its path.
Stood in the doorway of Joe Reed's locker room and turned Lori Dane away, saying Reed does not speak to interviewers before a pay-per-view, and gave her a comment on Kevin Slater and Tony Starks.
Walked Joe Reed to the ring for the World title cell match, holding his belt.

Came to the announce table in an Adidas warm-up top and USA Wrestling shorts to call the Myers match, argued with Todd Michaelson, left to fight Tony Starks in the aisle, and later cut a promo in the ring promising to take the World title from Tony Starks and Joe Reed.
Stepped through the curtain first, ahead of Chris Myers and Bobby Taylor, for the match against Tiger Claw.
Came to ringside with Chris Myers during the World title cell match.
Came to ringside with Dallas to even the odds for Kevin Slater in the cell and fought the Syndicate alongside Luke Steele.
Came out with Chris Myers and Dallas, stopped halfway down the aisle to keep Tiger Claw's allies out, and fought Casey James there.
After the match lay motionless; paramedics said his heart had stopped and gave him CPR as he was carried to the back, and the announcers did not know his condition.
Ran down the aisle to save Gabriel Whitecross, was chokeslammed through the announcers' table by Serge Annis, then threw himself on Whitecross's chest and DDT'd an attendant who tried to move him.

After the bell, chokeslammed Mark Langseth through the announcers' table; the announcers say Robert Donovan will meet him in the first match of the King of the Death Match tournament at the next An Evening To The Extreme.

Interviewed in his locker room by Lori Dane: said he spent twenty months in the IIWF, had come to the EMWC to start anew, that the attack on Whitecross was a message to everyone, and that he had spilled his first blood in the EMWC.
Appeared on top of the cell after the main event and set it on fire.
Walked the Fabulous Ones to the ring, told the male fans in the crowd what couch potatoes they were, and introduced Agito Nakajima and Sho Satsuma.
Slid a copy of the December 1997 Playboy issue featuring her through the cell bars to distract Chris O'Brien while Sho Satsuma attacked.
Followed Ms. Miki to the ring, helped her up the steps and stood by the press table with his arms crossed.
Introduced as the third special enforcer, "The Attack", in sparkling jacket and Oakley shades, to a huge pop.

Pulled Trey Porter off the apron to stop him tagging; after the match superkicked Christopher Stonebreaker, passed out Body Shop shirts and told the crowd the Body Shop was back with Trey Porter, Ronnie D and Simon Lebec.

Introduced as the second special enforcer to Lynyrd Skynyrd's "Gimme Back My Bullets" and stared down Christopher Stonebreaker; when Steve Spector's foot hit him on a plancha to the floor, he threw Spector and Simon Lebec back into the ring.
Tossed Simon Lebec back into the ring during the match; afterward cleared the ring with a chair, then hit Christopher Stonebreaker with it and told the crowd he was hired by Ronnie D and Lebec.
After the match, hugged Trey Porter and told the crowd the Snake Den and Porter had pretended to hate each other for near three months, mocking the Syndicate, the Cult of Personality and Joe Reed.
After the match told the crowd the Body Shop had fooled the whole federation, and handed the microphone to Trey Porter.
On Dan Oliver's right fist: talked smack to Curtis Hansen, argued with Oliver in the cell and was slapped across Hansen's chest for the pin that eliminated Hansen and Quigley.
Walked to ringside during the World title cell match, spoke to Brian Lau and clapped Casey James on the back, and laughed at Joe Reed in Tony Starks's chokehold.
Grinned when Kevin Slater hit the Floating DDT on Joe Reed, floored Brian Lau with a right hand and fought the Syndicate with Chris Myers; Todd Michaelson says Steele taught Slater the move.

matches.stipulation: EMWC Junior Heavyweight Title Tournament, semifinal; one fall, twenty-minute time limit
matches.note: Brown comes out dancing with a woman at ringside to Basic Connection's "Habla Me Luna" while Mota, to Sepultura's "The Great Southern Trendkill", dropkicks him off the apron into the guardrail. Brown answers with a Northern Lights suplex, a leg lariat, a vertical suplex and a release German suplex; Mota hits an Asai moonsault onto the concrete, whips Brown into the ring post, then hurts his knee falling from the top rope when he goes for the Main Attraction and fights on injured. Brown survives a float-over DDT and Mota's elbow drop, Mota kicks out of a Running Lyger Bomb and of a Michinoku Driver II into a piledriver, and Brown wins with an Exploder suplex into the Harle-Quinn from the top rope. Mota is helped to the back for an MRI on his knee.

matches.stipulation: EMWC Television Title (Sinister defending)
matches.note: Paragon, in a half-face red mask, enters to Skid Row's "Youth Gone Wild" and Sinister, to S.D.B.B.'s "Pride", runs straight in. Sinister takes a dropkick to the knees, then pulverizes Paragon with punches, a missile dropkick, ring-post slams, a powerslam and a ten-punch count on the buckles before a Camel Clutch. Paragon rakes his eyes and locks on a Boston Crab; Sinister hits Thunderstruck and covers, but the referee stops the count as a cage holding Lady Apocalypse is lowered above the ring. Paragon hits Sinister with the title belt, covers and wins the title as the cage settles inches away. After the bell Sinister beats Paragon down with the belt and leaves with his wife.

matches.stipulation: EMWC Junior Heavyweight Title Tournament, semifinal; one fall
matches.note: Claw comes out with Brian Lau to Faith No More's "The Art of Making Enemies"; Infierno's father Volatil Pesadilla is at ringside. Claw floors Infierno with a kick flurry, wheel kicks and a Syndi-Cutter on the floor and locks on a kataha jime; the referee lifts and drops Infierno's arm twice, then a third time Infierno lifts it himself and works free to a sleeper and a backflip. Claw hits a Death Valley Driver and a brainbuster, but when he sets up a Syndi-Cutter from the turnbuckles Infierno has hooked his own legs in the ropes and Claw falls on his head. Infierno lands Fire in the Sky and rolls Claw up with a La Majistral cradle for the three.

matches.stipulation: Triple threat match, one fall, thirty-minute time limit; the winner to get a Television Title shot against Paragon at the first An Evening To The Extreme after the pay-per-view
matches.note: James rides to the ring on a sedated bull to Aerosmith's "Walk This Way", Hell enters to AC/DC's "Highway to Hell" and Bryant comes out with Glory and Elena to "Big Gun". Hell lands Death's Cradle on James but the referee, Eobard Majors, breaks the count when Elena climbs on the apron and bares her chest; Bryant uses a chain from his kneepad for a loaded kneedrop, and the three trade a double flying lariat and chokeshots. When Hell lifts Bryant for his brainbuster Bryant slides out and kicks him with Call Me in the Morning for the three. James then takes the microphone and challenges Bryant to finish it one on one, and Bryant pins him again with the Ultimate Prescription.

matches.stipulation: Tag Team Grudge Match under Texas Death Match rules, announced by Kuyler Greyson: no disqualification, no countout and, for Quigley, no submission; a pinned man must not rise by a count of ten
matches.note: Hansen, limping on a kneebrace after a brawl at a wedding, comes out to "Franchise Players" carrying a sign mocking the Predators and cuts a promo on the microphone, then Quigley comes out to AC/DC's "For Those About to Rock". Bear and Phoenix beat Hansen down with a bearhug, a double powerbomb and a spiked piledriver while Quigley refuses the tag; after Hansen's Thunderstryker Quigley comes in, and Hansen and Quigley hit a double suplex, double dropkicks and a snap superplex that Bear breaks up. Quigley chairs Bear and locks him in the Vindicator while Hansen drives Phoenix through a table with the ThunderBomb and pins him; the referee counts ten and Hansen and Quigley win.

matches.stipulation: Battle of the Managers
matches.note: The Natural Predators are in Greyson's corner and Tiger Claw and Casey James in Lau's. Greyson works Lau's leg with an anklelock and a standing figure four, while Lau scores with an eyerake, kicks and chops and misses a Blackheart Punch. A brawl breaks out outside: Tony Starks and Hakiro Matsuoko run in and are jumped by Quinn Brown and Kabuki Kid, and the Fabulous Ones, Agito Nakajima and Sho Satsuma, join in. President Chris Blue climbs in with a chair meant for Lau; Lau pulls Greyson into its path, Tiger Claw puts Lau on the knocked-out Greyson, and when Starks throws the referee back in he sees Lau's guillotine chokehold and calls the bell, announced as a win by referee's decision.

matches.stipulation: Special grudge match, one fall, forty-five-minute time limit
matches.note: Referee Jimmy Storm sends Tiger Claw's manager Brian Lau and Myers's manager Dallas to the outside; Bobby Taylor stops halfway down the aisle to keep Claw's allies out. Claw takes over with kicks, a Step Up Enzugiri and a Syndicutter that also knocks out the referee, and Casey James comes out and is met by Taylor. Claw hits a Golden Tiger Strike for a two count, and Myers ducks a shin kick and hits the Rattler, both men down for the referee's count; Myers holds the ropes when Claw jumps from the second rope for another Syndicutter and wins with a tornado-style Rattler off the second rope for the three, as Tony Starks and Kevin Slater fight in the aisle.

matches.stipulation: EMWC North American Title (Whitecross defending); one fall, sixty-minute time limit; the challenger kept secret
matches.note: Whitecross enters first to Nuclear Assault's "Something Wicked"; Ken Graham reacts in disbelief before announcing the challenger, Serge Annis, making his EMWC debut to "Hands of Death". Annis floors the champion with clotheslines and a plancha and sends him into the steel rail; Whitecross answers with a drop toe hold, a kneebreaker and a leg lock, then locks on the Sacred Tailsman STF, which Annis muscles out of. Whitecross hits Annis twice in the head with a steel chair and Annis stays on his feet, then hits the Epitomizer chokeslam three times and a fourth after the referee warns him he will be disqualified; the referee calls the bell and Whitecross keeps the title.

matches.stipulation: One fall; the match leaves the ring and the arena floor
matches.note: James comes out with Brian Lau and a bottle of Kessler's whiskey to "Foul Taste of Freedom"; Taylor, from Tombstone, Arizona, has his wife and son at ringside. Taylor hits a superplex turned neckbreaker, a lariat that sends James into the ring steps, a piledriver on the steps, a Cajun Mojo Dropper and a backward leap from the apron through a table. They fight through the stadium: James drags Taylor up to the 300 level and throws him in a military press; Taylor does the same to James, locks him in a locker in a locker room and smashes it with a sledgehammer, and carries him back for a pin that James kicks out of. James smashes the whiskey bottle across Taylor's head and covers for the three, then sets the soaked Taylor on fire.

matches.stipulation: EMWC Junior Heavyweight Title Tournament, final; one fall, sixty-minute time limit; for the vacant title
matches.note: Brown offers a handshake at the bell. Infierno, giving away six inches and about fifty pounds, uses an armdrag, a backflip and a flying axe kick; Brown answers with a hurricanrana, a DDT, a somersault legdrop and a tombstone. Infierno hits a Shooting Star Press to the floor, a corkscrew plancha and a 450 splash, Brown a baseball slide, a Running Liger Bomb and a guillotine legdrop, and Brown hurts his knee on the steel. Up on the top rope Infierno chops Brown in the throat and hits a Super Death Valley Driver for the three, and is named the new EMWC Junior Heavyweight Champion. Brown is helped to the back with Kuyler Greyson.

matches.stipulation: EMWC World Tag Team Titles (the Fraternity Boys defending), Hell On Earth: four teams, elimination rules, inside a steel cell
matches.note: Ms. Miki, with Jack Banks behind her, introduces the Fabulous Ones; the Down Boys come out with the glove Jivvy; the Fraternity Boys crowd-surf to the ring with a shopping cart of weapons and Chris O'Brien smashes a bottle on his own forehead. Hansen and Dan Oliver start the match; the Frat Boys hit the Initiation on Oliver but a bottle thrown by Peterson knocks Gus out. Ms. Miki slides a Playboy issue through the bars to distract O'Brien, Sho Satsuma dropkicks him into the steel, and Satsuma hits Zampitella with a camera and eliminates him with a Kamikaze Slam. Hansen and Quigley fall out when Quigley chairs Hansen, piledrives him on the chair and leaves, and Oliver slaps Jivvy across Hansen's chest for the three. The Down Boys then beat the Fabulous Ones, Peterson hitting a legdrop and Oliver a moonsault on Sho Satsuma for the three.

matches.stipulation: Grudge Tag Team Match, one fall; Christopher Stonebreaker, "Cowboy" Ken Curtis and Zack Malone as special guest enforcers outside the ring
matches.note: Lebec and Ronnie D, the Snake Den, face Spector and Porter, who returns after two years. Stonebreaker pulls Ronnie D off the apron and throws Lebec back in, Curtis tosses Spector and Lebec back in, and Malone pulls Porter off the apron so he cannot tag. The Snake Den work Spector over with double teams, a Heartbreaker through a table by Ronnie D and a rocker dropper while Spector hits a front layout, a missile dropkick, an Asai moonsault, a somersault legdrop on a chair and a Cherry Blossom Bomber. Porter breaks Spector's cover on Lebec, superkicks Lebec, then hits Spector with the Heartbreaker, and Ronnie D covers Spector for the three. Porter, Ronnie D, Lebec and Malone embrace and beat down Spector and Stonebreaker, and Curtis clears the ring with a chair and then hits Stonebreaker with it.

matches.stipulation: EMWC World Heavyweight Championship (Reed defending); triangle match inside a steel cell, no time limit, countouts or disqualifications; a man is eliminated by pinfall, submission or knockout and the last man left wins the title
matches.note: Slater enters to Sevendust's "Black", Starks with Brian Lau to Led Zeppelin's "Kashmir", and Reed with the Lady in Red to Bad Company's "Bad Company", climbing the cell for a cross body block on both. Casey James and Hakiro Matsuoko, Chris Myers with Dallas, and Luke Steele come to ringside in turn. Starks chairs Reed, Reed superbombs Starks through a table, Slater moonsaults onto both, Starks chokes Reed with a table leg, and Reed drives Starks through the cell door; Slater leaps from halfway up the cell and then from its roof through the announcers' table. Slater pins Reed with a Floating DDT, eliminating him; Tiger Claw, disguised as the cell cameraman, hits Slater with the camera and shin-kicks Starks by mistake, and Slater counters Starks's kataha jime with a Swinging Ace Crusher for the three and the World Heavyweight Championship.

notes: The EMWC pay-per-view of 9 August 1998 from Texas Stadium in Irving, Texas, posted on 10 August 1998 in thirteen parts, with Jon Stegglet, Todd Michaelson and Richard "Moxy" Blue at the announce table, Ken Graham announcing, Jon Keeton and Lori Dane interviewing and Mike Barnes refereeing the main events. Thirteen matches are worked: the Junior Heavyweight Title Tournament semifinals and final, in which Juvenil Infierno beats Tiger Claw and then Quinn Brown to become the first Junior Heavyweight Champion; Paragon takes the Television Title from Sinister; Dave Bryant wins a triple threat; Curtis Hansen and Chris Quigley win a Texas Death Match over the Natural Predators; Brian Lau beats Kuyler Greyson; Chris Myers beats Tiger Claw; Gabriel Whitecross keeps the North American Title when Serge Annis, in his debut, is disqualified; Casey James beats Bobby Taylor and sets him on fire; the Down Boys win the Hell On Earth cell for the World Tag Team Titles; the Snake Den beat Steve Spector and Trey Porter as Porter, Zack Malone and Ken Curtis show themselves to be with the Body Shop; and Kevin Slater wins the World Heavyweight Championship in a cell. A replay of Showtime V is shown in part ten.

name: An Evening To The Extreme

date.source: The card's own heading, in the lines at the head of part one: An Evening To The Extreme, Septmeber 9, 1998, live from Wembley Stadium, Wembley, Great Britain.

appearances.note: At the announce table with Jon Stegglet and Todd Michaelson through the card, opening in the Paris sketch with a Coke in an Eiffel Tower cup; he falls asleep on the table during the North American Title match and hides under it during the tag title match.

Opened the show with the World title belt on his shoulder, said he would wrestle that night after all and added himself to the main event of Simon Lebec against Tiger Claw, making it a three-way dance for the title.

Came out in street clothes, took the house microphone and called Christopher Stonebreaker to the ring to answer for the Blood, Sweat, and Tears chair shot and for the week before; the two fought until security separated them.

Walked down the entrance ramp during the Stonebreaker and Quigley match; Stonebreaker stopped to wave him in and the referee went to the ropes to send him back, which let Quigley take Stonebreaker's sledgehammer to his knee.

Called out by Ken Curtis, was held by security halfway down the ramp, answered the demand for an apology with "I'm sorry that I didn't get the opportunity to finish knocking the living daylights out of you", broke free and traded punches with Curtis until security separated them.

Came to the aisle with a chair during the North American Title match and, while the referee checked on Mark Langseth, slid into the ring and hit Ken Curtis over the head with it, which let Langseth score the DDT and the three count.
Got into the ring with his bodyguard Crash after Curtis Hansen and Sam Hell had entered, offered Hell a handful of money, and walked away when Hell turned it down.
Knocked Sam Hell to the canvas with a big right hand when Hell turned down Mike Sebastian's money, drove in stomps and stepped out to the floor before the Hansen match began.

Came out with Elena and Glory carrying the RMWA and GFWA World Heavyweight Titles beside the EMWC Television Title, boasted of being a champion in two other feds, mocked Sinister and said Sinister should call him in the morning.
Walked arm in arm with Dave Bryant in a blue silk dress, carrying the GFWA World Heavyweight Title.
Tended to Bryant outside the ring and was knocked down with a lariat by a woman in a Paragon t-shirt.
Walked arm in arm with Dave Bryant in short jean shorts and a half-shirt, carrying the RMWA World Heavyweight Title.
Tended to Bryant outside the ring and screamed when Elena was hit with a lariat by a woman in a Paragon t-shirt.

Entered the ring in his suit, said Hakiro had retired and Starks wanted to do his own thing so that the EMWC Syndicate was outnumbered, challenged Kevin Slater to come and fight him, claimed an undefeated record, stripped to the waist and left.
Came to the ring with Tiger Claw for the World title triangle match.
Sneaked around the corner during the triangle match and drove Kevin Slater's face into the ring apron; Luke Steele chased him off.
Appeared in the four-way tag match highlights, went to the top rope and hit Kyle Lee with a Kamikaze Drop, then left; the announcers ask whether there is a past between the Kid and Lee.
Came into the ring after the four-way tag match and laid into the Benjamins with Randall Osbourne.
Shown in a backstage promo telling Luke Steele that a wrong opponent throws off a game plan, naming the Blackheart Punch and the Black Death as his moves and defending Derek Mota and Tony Starks.
Lay unconscious in the ring after the lights went out for the second week running, a burning Syndicate shirt beside him and a Cult of Personality shirt over his face.
Came out to Van Halen's "Fire in the Hole", announced that he was in the EMWC, challenged "Bad Boy" Mark Bagwell, insulted the MLWO, lit a joint and burned an MLWO shirt in the ring.

Shown in a taped scene at LAX with Jensei Tenru, back in the US from Tokyo, described as an IIWF Hall of Famer and former Syndicate member; tells a customs guard that he is Tenru's manager and that Tenru will compete in the EMWC.
Shown in a taped scene at LAX arguing with a customs guard, calling himself Hakiro Matsuoko's number one protege and the heir to his legacy, and signing a stranger's passport.
Came to the ring behind Matt Harris holding the gold-plated cheese grater and carrying a black duffel bag, and handed over the grater and the weapons during the match.

After the bell caught a camera operator by the lapels, shouted that he would get Annis next time and that Blue had a lot of explaining to do, and gave the man a Super Death Valley Driver off the top rope until security pulled him away.
Shown in a backstage clip before the Spector match quoting 1 Samuel 24:20, calling himself the man who would be King of the Death Match and telling Spector there would be no comeback this time.
Led the Down Boys to the ring, carrying a baseball bat.

Came out to the Beastie Boys with Ronnie D, Billy Sexton, Zack Malone and Trey Porter, took the microphone to say he had beaten Slater and still got no gold, called Tiger Claw an insignificant bug, and promised to beat Claw that night and then Slater.
Came out with the Body Shop behind Simon Lebec for his promo.
Came out with the Body Shop behind Simon Lebec for his promo.
Came out with the Body Shop behind Simon Lebec for his promo.
Came out with the Body Shop behind Simon Lebec, introduced as the crazy man from Wawa.
Came to the ring by Simon Lebec's side for the triangle match.
Hit Kevin Slater on the knee with a steel chair out of the referee's sight during the triangle match, and was floored by Luke Steele's right hand and a clothesline over the railing.

Came out through four walls of flame without being scheduled, shoved an official down, took the microphone from Ken Graham, thanked Robert Donovan for the barbed-wire welcome, said Gabrielle Whitecross had paid with his life, told Mark Langseth he would fail his master, and challenged anyone in the back to answer him.

Answered Serge Annis's open challenge from the entrance in a French national soccer jersey, told him he did not scare him, recalled Annis's losses to J.W. Hardin and to a man with a red eye patch, and accepted a match for that night.

Rushed from the crowd with a chair to hit Serge Annis in revenge for his mentor, hit Chris Myers by mistake when Annis ducked, was slammed with the Epitomizer, and afterwards hit the unconscious Myers with the chair and folded it round his ankle until Luke Steele pulled him away.
Came through the crowd with Dallas, pulled Mark Langseth off Chris Myers, and walked backstage after the ambulance left.

Came down the aisle bandaged from the James match, floored Billy Sexton with a right hand and a clothesline over the railing, chased Brian Lau away, clotheslined Simon Lebec and threw Tiger Claw back into the ring, then talked to the injured Kevin Slater.
Came through the crowd with Luke Steele, knelt by the stricken Chris Myers and went with him in the ambulance.
Eliminated from the Junior Heavyweight triangle match, then hit from behind as he went up the aisle with a toolbox and a slab of ice by a masked man, who left him motionless.

Came through the curtain in a shark-tooth muzzle mask after Derek Mota's elimination from the Junior Heavyweight triangle match, threw a toolbox onto Mota's head and then into his back, broke a slab of ice over his head, said it did not matter whether he was Simon Ezra or still the Blood Angel, and was announced for a death match against Mota the next week.

Took the microphone from Ken Graham before the main event and said that wrestlers are paid to lose and the business is an angle; when his microphone was cut he grabbed Jon Stegglet over the table, struck a security guard in the throat and choked a fan unconscious with a guillotine until security pulled him off; Stegglet says it will be the last time he is seen on an EMWC show.

matches.stipulation: Four-way tag team match, one fall; the first team to score a pin or a submission wins
matches.note: Shown in part two as highlights of a match held before the broadcast: the Fabulous Ones, the Benjamins, Anarchy and the team of Kyle Lee and Randall Osbourne. Osbourne and Agito Nakajima are about to collide when Osbourne tags in Lee, who hops in and is hit with a boot to the gut and the Road to Nowhere DDT by his own partner; Anarchy swarms the ring and attacks Osbourne and Agito, Sho Satsuma comes in, and the Kabuki Kid hits Lee with a Kamikaze Drop from the top and leaves; Bobby Benjamin covers Lee while his brother spins the referee around for the three. Jack Banks and Osbourne then lay into the Benjamins. The page names none of Anarchy's members and not the second Benjamin, who are not entered.

matches.stipulation: Triangle match to name the number one contender to the Junior Heavyweight Title
matches.note: Held before the broadcast and shown in part seven as highlights: the Kabuki Kid goes to the top rope and hits Mota with a Kamikaze Drop for the three, eliminating him; as Mota walks up the aisle he is hit with a toolbox and a slab of ice by a masked man (see the Simon Ezra angle); in the finish Quinn Brown reverses a Kabuki Kid powerbomb into a rollup for the win. Brown becomes the number one contender to the Junior Heavyweight Title; the champion, Juvenil Infierno, offers to shake his hand and Brown refuses.

matches.stipulation: One fall, twenty-minute time limit
matches.note: Ken Graham announces in French. After both men have entered, Mike Sebastian and his bodyguard Crash, the Dead Presidents, get into the ring, Sebastian offers Hell a handful of money and Crash knocks Hell down with a right hand and stomps before the bell. Hell takes Hansen down with forearms, an elbow drop and a figure-four attempt, and works Hansen's leg with stomps and a legdrop; Hansen answers with a drop toe hold, a spinebuster, suplexes, a Floating DDT and the Thunder Bomb for the three. After the bell he applies a hangman's noose and will not let go until security pulls him off; Hell is helped to the back.

matches.stipulation: EMWC North American Title (Mark Langseth defending in place of Gabriel Whitecross); one fall
matches.note: Ken Graham introduces Curtis as a former SCRA and NLWP World Champion twice over and the winner of the Night of Glory battle royal, from Dripping Springs, Texas, and Langseth from Pittsburgh as the man defending Gabriel Whitecross's title. Langseth takes out Curtis's knee at the bell; Curtis takes over with a lariat, a shoulderbreaker, a tilt-a-whirl backbreaker, a spinebuster and a flying lariat to the floor, and spits on Langseth, who answers with a piledriver, a dragon screw legwhip, an ankle lock, a cross body and a reversed Cowboy-plex into a front layout suplex. Curtis sends Langseth into the ring steps and powerslams him on the floor; as the referee checks on Langseth, Christopher Stonebreaker slides in and hits Curtis with a chair, and Langseth hits a DDT and covers him for the three.

matches.stipulation: EMWC World Television Title (Dave Bryant defending); one fall
matches.note: Sinister, from Chicago, comes out to S.D.B.B.'s "Pride" without Lady Apocalypse, reported in hospital, and Dave Bryant, from Las Vegas, to AC/DC's "Big Gun" with Elena and Glory. Sinister dominates early with rights, a military press held nearly ten seconds, a fallaway slam, a sidewalk slam, a front-facelock DDT and an overhead German release suplex; Bryant answers with kicks, a piledriver, a flying legdrop, a bulldog attempt that Sinister turns into a crotching on the turnbuckle, and a small package. As Sinister sets up the Thunderstruck piledriver a woman in a "Paragon" t-shirt appears and lariats Elena outside; the referee breaks the count, and Bryant superkicks Sinister and pins him with Call Me In The Morning. Ken Graham announces Bryant as still champion.

matches.stipulation: One fall, twenty-minute time limit
matches.note: After a backstage promo by James, Referee Alain LeGros oversees the match. Steele, from Cleveland at 275 pounds, comes out in Cult of Personality gear to "I am the Man" and holds up a fan's sign; James, at 340 pounds from Parts Unknown, is drenched with a fan's soda, tears the sign and bull-rushes the ring. Steele starts with a drop toe hold and kicks; James takes over with a scoop slam, a choke he passes off as a nerve pinch, a spinebuster and a rolling neckbreaker; Steele comes back with armdrags, a Moxykick dropkick that sends James over the top, a running bulldog and a suplex release onto a steel chair, then a Floating DDT and the Cattle Buster for the three. He drapes his Cult of Personality shirt over the face of the unconscious James as the lights go out.

matches.stipulation: King of the Death Match tournament, round one; Taipei Death Match, falls count anywhere in the stadium; one fall
matches.note: Ken Graham announces a Taipei Death Match where falls will count anywhere in Wembley; Chris Staley, from Wildwood, New Jersey, makes his EMWC debut and his opponent is a mystery until Matt Harris, from New York, arrives with Sydney. With glass wrapped on their hands they brawl through the arena: Harris cuts Staley with a backhand and headbutts and hits a spinning backfist and a suicide dive; Staley hits a springboard Asai moonsault, a Russian legsweep into the barricade, a springboard enzuigiri, a DDT off the top, and a sitdown faceslam; Harris uses a toaster and its cord, a steel chair, a legdrop on the chair, the gold-plated cheese grater and the fans' shots, and wins with the Harris Special, a running bulldog onto the grater, after Staley's leap through a table misses.

matches.stipulation: EMWC World Tag Team Titles (the Down Boys defending); one fall, thirty-minute time limit
matches.note: The Fracas Boys of Stockholm enter to the Twilight Zone theme and the Down Boys, the reigning champions, to Warrant's "Down Boys" led by Awesome T. Kristof dropkicks Oliver, Peterson hits a cross body and a spinning heel kick, Creed clotheslines Peterson, smashes Oliver's head into the turnbuckle for a ten count and spinebusters him on the concrete, and the pair hit Peterson with a legdrop off the top; Peterson hits a double clothesline, Oliver a neckbreaker, a nerve hold and a tilt-a-whirl backbreaker. Oliver rolls up Kristof Johanssan and Adrienne Creed breaks up the pin a second too late, so the Down Boys retain.

matches.stipulation: One fall, thirty-minute time limit
matches.note: Quigley, from Chicago at 241 pounds, offers to shake hands at the bell and Stonebreaker, from Lafayette, Louisiana at 265, takes it. Quigley works Stonebreaker's arm and then his knee with a kneebar, a figure-four, a kneebreaker and a Fujiwara armbar on the knee, between a dragon suplex and a fisherman buster; Stonebreaker reverses the figure-four, hits a belly-to-belly, a DDT and a powerslam, and signals for the Rockslide Suplex when Ken Curtis walks down the ramp. While the referee warns Curtis off, Quigley hits Stonebreaker's knee with his sledgehammer and pins him with a rolling cradle. Stonebreaker is taken out on a stretcher.

matches.stipulation: King of the Death Match tournament, round one; Texas Death Match, barbed wire ropes and broken glass surrounding the ring; ten-count
matches.note: Caleb Temple, from Trinity, South Carolina, and "Armitage" Steve Spector, from Carteret, New Jersey, who is going for his 100th win and has lost to Temple three times before; Referee Mike Barnes counts. Temple opens with a plancha off a ladder; Spector answers with a power-rana counter that spikes Temple's head on a chair and a somersault plancha, and the pair use the railing, chairs, a table, a ladder, the glass and the barbed wire. Spector hits a moonsault DDT into the glass, a Shooting Star Press with a chair through a table, a Springboard Arabian facebuster and a Diamond Cutter onto a chair; Temple hits a split-legged tombstone in the glass, a powerbomb on the ladder, the Last Rites scorpion deathlock, a diving headbutt and, on top of a ladder, a tornado DDT that leaves both men down. Both crawl to the ropes and pull themselves up, one falls back, and the ten count ends it; Ken Graham announces Temple the winner, who moves on to round two.

matches.stipulation: One fall
matches.note: An impromptu match with Dick Longfellow refereeing from the ring. Annis comes out first, from Oakville, Ontario at 6 foot 8 and 290 pounds, and waits halfway up the aisle for Chris Myers, who runs out without his music. They brawl through the front rows: a back body drop and a clothesline for Annis, a standing dropkick and a splash on chairs and a spinebuster on the railing for Myers; Annis hits a crotch slam, a pancake and a splash on the steps. Mark Langseth rushes from the crowd to hit Annis with a chair and hits Myers by mistake; Annis hits the Epitomizer on Langseth and then the Double Epitomizer on Langseth and Myers, and leaves. Langseth hits Myers with the chair again and tries to break his ankle in the folded chair until Luke Steele and Dallas pull him off; Myers is taken away in an ambulance. No winner is announced.

matches.stipulation: EMWC Heavyweight Championship of the World (Kevin Slater defending); triangle match, first pin wins, all three men in at once
matches.note: Lebec, with Billy Sexton, enters to the Beastie Boys, Tiger Claw, with Brian Lau, to Faith No More, and Slater last, to Sevendust's "Black"; Lebec drops an elbow on Slater as he slides in. Claw hits Lebec and Slater with kicks, a head-and-arm suplex, a German suplex and a guillotine legdrop over the railing; Slater hits a somersault plancha but his left knee gives way and Claw attacks it with a Muay Thai kick and a spinning toe hold. Lebec hits a DDT, a piledriver and the Antagonist on the knee; Sexton hits Slater's knee with a chair and Brian Lau drives his face into the apron until Luke Steele clears both. Claw hits a front layout superplex and the Golden Tiger Strike but Slater makes the save; Lebec backdrops Claw to the floor and goes for Slater, who counters with a Northern Lights Bomb and pins Lebec to keep the title.

notes: The EMWC television show An Evening To The Extreme of 9 September 1998 from Wembley Stadium in Wembley, Great Britain, posted on 14 September 1998 in eight parts, the first stop of the EMWC World Tour, with Jon Stegglet, Todd Michaelson and Richard "Moxy" Blue at the announce table and Ken Graham announcing. Twelve matches are worked, two of them in highlights from before the broadcast: the Benjamins win a four-way tag match; Quinn Brown wins a Junior Heavyweight triangle; Curtis Hansen beats Sam Hell; Mark Langseth keeps the North American Title over Ken Curtis with help from Christopher Stonebreaker; Dave Bryant keeps the Television Title over Sinister; Luke Steele beats Casey James; Matt Harris beats Chris Staley in a Taipei Death Match; the Down Boys keep the World Tag Team Titles over the Fracas Boys; Chris Quigley beats Stonebreaker; Caleb Temple beats Steve Spector in a Texas Death Match; Chris Myers and Serge Annis brawl with no result announced; and Kevin Slater pins Simon Lebec in a three-way for the World title. Parts of the text keep the previous week's French dateline (a Paris sketch, French announcements, the Palais de Sports and a French crowd); the card's own heading gives Wembley Stadium.

name: An Evening To The Extreme

date.source: The subject lines of the operator's note and of part one, which head the card 'An Evening To The Extreme (Sept. 30)'; the year is the year of posting (7 October 1998), and the pages name the Tokyo Dome.

appearances.note: Arrives at the red carpet on a vintage Harley Davidson that he says was Dennis Hopper's bike in Easy Rider, and, asked about the Annis attacks, says he will bring a flashlight to the ring if Annis comes down with the lights off.

Backstage, hits Luke Steele on the back and head and Chris Myers on the back with a steel chair, says he is 'taking advantage of a good situation', and fights Serge Annis until officials separate them.
His motorcycle burns and blows up in the parking lot, and a driverless car with a lever on the pedal races at him; he dives clear, and a Syndicate shirt is found burning on the driver's seat.
Arrives at the red carpet in a white limousine to a big pop and tells Lori Dane to keep her eyes on him that night.

After the opening match runs in with a fire extinguisher and sprays Jensei Tenru and Hakiro Matsuoko in the crotch, challenges Tenru to a Mexican Death Match the next week in Mexico City with Juvenil Infierno as the padlocked door, and sprays Tenru and Matsuoko again.
In the ring with Jensei Tenru when Quinn Brown attacks with a fire extinguisher after the opening match.
Addressed by Quinn Brown after the opening match, who tells him to stay down and to get his father to advise him on the man he treated like trash.

Limps to the ring with the World Title on his shoulder and says he has two matches that night, against Brian Lau and, in an Iron Man match, Curtis Hansen; says he is wrestling on a bad knee, that it is the last match for one of them, and tells Hansen to bring his best for his last ride and his last walk on the wild side.
In a taped locker-room scene beside El Vampyro, announces that the pair will take the EMWC tag team titles and tells the Tokyo Kid and Fuji they will be Bloodstorm's first victims.

Walks out to a standing ovation in new trunks reading 'Tradition' with the international symbol for 'no', tells the fan holding a 'WORKRATE' sign that he will get what the sign wants in a few hours, calls the Iron Man the final match between him and Kevin Slater, and, turning to the rumours of his retirement, drops the microphone without answering.
With his brother Anthony Logan, enters after the Bloodstorm match, stomps Bloodstorm and takes the microphone: 'We're back!'.
Hits Bobby Storm and El Vampyro with the Dragonstrike Heart Punch and speaks to the Fraternity Boys through the microphone.

Described in the recap of the Television Title match: a new wrestler in the EMWC, he races down the aisle after Bryant's win, assaults the fallen Paragon and puts him through a table with the Love Bug.
Knocked out by Dave Bryant's chair, then assaulted by Edward Love and put through a table with the Love Bug; he is carried out on a stretcher, and early reports say he may never wrestle again.

During the North American Title match the lights flicker and his voice dares Langseth to look up; a dummy dressed as Gabriel Whitecross hangs from the catwalk in a noose and burns, Annis takes Langseth's chains from the timekeeper's table, soaks them in kerosene, sets them on fire at the aisle and clotheslines and Epitomizes Langseth on the floor while Myers lies in the ring.

Backstage with Lori Dane, says he took away Langseth's belt as well as Whitecross's health, mentions Robert Donovan, says the Tokyo Dome has never seen him and promises to Epitomize his way past two tired men in the triangle match.
Comes to the ramp after Myers wins the title, cuts the music and orders a rematch later that night in a triangle match among Myers, Langseth and Serge Annis.
Comes to the ring to the sound of Beck's 'Where It's At' and refuses the Fraternity Boys' lawyer, saying they stay suspended indefinitely until he is shown a court order.
Lowered over the ring hanging from a wooden crucifix, he recites verses and vanishes in smoke and explosions, leaving the crucifix standing in the ring.
During Slater's match against Brian Lau argues with the referee from the apron, pushes Lau out of Slater's Wild Ride spin and knocks Slater out with a shin kick, setting up Lau's pinfall.

Walks out backwards in a Toronto Maple Leafs jersey and talks about the Body Shop reuniting, the Body Shop's four members, Christopher Stonebreaker, Steve Spector and Ken Curtis, and says 'Felix was screwed'.
Comes to the ring after the WarGames, helps Trey Porter to his feet, and hits Ronnie D with a chair in the beating that follows.
After the tag match comes back with a chair and hits Charles Scheffield on the back of the head, then Sam Hell, and hammers Hell's knee.

Walks to the ring to Prince's 'Kiss' in a white fur coat and sky blue silk shirt with a woman on each arm, says he signed with the EMWC, mocks the Extreme tournament as a disgrace, and says EMWC now stands for 'Earnin' Money With Coules'.
Introduces Kabuki Kid for the Junior Heavyweight Title match with Jack Banks beside her, and later the Fabulous Ones for the tag title match.
After the Fabulous Ones win, speaks for the Daimyo and offers Dave Bryant a place in it as a brother.

Stands at ringside with his arms crossed beside Ms. Miki for the Junior Heavyweight Title match and again for the tag title match; during the tag title match he turns toward the announce table and arches an eyebrow at Todd Michaelson, who has just said he will sit back and watch Miki.
Goes to the ring on Dan Oliver's fist, argues with Oliver over who should start, hits Sho Satsuma in the crotch and trips him during the Down Boys' work on him.

Argues with Ms. Miki at ringside, leaves, then jumps the guardrail onto the apron during the tag title match and superkicks Adam Peterson off the top turnbuckle while the referee is distracted, setting up the Fabulous Ones' win.
After the Fabulous Ones' win, takes the microphone and says the only thing the Daimyo is missing is the Doctor of Love; Randall Osbourne welcomes him to the flock.
Slides into the ring after the WarGames and hits Ronnie D with a double superkick with Trey Porter.
Comes to the ring with Kabuki Kid and Tawni, takes the microphone from Dave Bryant, kisses Tawni of the Nasty Habits and welcomes Bryant to the Daimyo.
Comes down the aisle with Kabuki Kid and Randall Osbourne, is kissed by Osbourne when he consults his partner on whether the Daimyo needs a Doctor of Love.
Climbs into the ring as the Fraternity Boys' lawyer to demand their reinstatement and is turned down by Chris Blue.
With Zombie, runs down the aisle with chairs and brutalizes the fans called Greece during a fight in the stands; cuts his own forehead with a broken bottle.
With MadDog, runs down the aisle with chairs and attacks Greece, then takes a microphone, presents the Vogon Poet's Guild and asks for O'Brien and Zampitella to be brought back.

Returns to a standing ovation to Nuclear Assault's 'Something Wicked', thanks Mark Langseth for defending his title and asks for it back; Langseth gives him the belt, kicks him and DDTs him, and Whitecross rises, punches Langseth, chokeslams him and locks on the Family Name ankle lock before Langseth kicks him in the groin and applies his own ankle lock.

After winning the North American Title again takes the microphone, hands Gabriel Whitecross the belt, kicks and DDTs him, tells him he wasted three months on him and that Annis should have finished him, and leaves with the belt.
Arrives in the back where Myers lies on the floor and Annis holds a steel chair, leaps on Annis and punches him in the face.
Struck across the back and head with a steel chair by Casey James and slumps to the floor.
Hit across the back with a steel chair by Casey James as he climbs to his feet.
In a taped scene on a Japanese wooden bridge with a girl beside him, tells Caleb the fable of the scorpion and the frog and says the operative phrase this time is 'fear for yourself'.

Returns, bloodied and broken, after the Killing Box, runs down the ramp to springboard-dropkick Tony Starks and slashes his forehead with a blade, then tells him that reality is coming for him and that pain is real and he is pain.

In a taped backstage promo, in a soft Southern drawl, says the King of the Death Match is the last mountain, that he does not want to be remembered for what he did to 'Offensive' Alex Adams or Steve Sampson, and that he will break Simon Ezra into a thousand pieces.
In a taped backstage scene tuning a guitar, talks about the Triple Cage Tower and names Casey James, Derek Mota, Luke Steele, Tiger Claw, Ken Curtis and Christopher Stonebreaker as the men in it.
Walks Chris Staley to the ring in an EMWC T-shirt and slaps hands with the fans.
Hits Christopher Stonebreaker on the back of the head with a steel chair on the ramp, slams his head into the railing and throws him into the cage before the bell.

In a locker-room scene with earplugs in, tells Lori Dane the Body Shop act like children, that he is a wrestler and an adult, and that he and Spector, Quinn Brown and the mystery partner will win the WarGames.

Takes off his headset at the announce table, walks to the ramp and is revealed, to 'I Love Rock and Roll' in karaoke style with 'MYSTERY SOLVED' painted on his chest, as the mystery partner returning to the ring.
After the WarGames, is slapped by Trey Porter, fights back, and is beaten by Porter, Drago, Zack Malone, Dave Bryant and Derek Mota; he is carried out on a stretcher.
After the WarGames, screams at Ronnie D and slaps him, takes the microphone to invite the locker room to take its shots, and joins in the beating with Drago, Malone, Dave Bryant and Derek Mota.
Climbs into the ring to chokeslam Ronnie D twice, the second after the others have finished.
Joins the beating of Ronnie D after the WarGames with a chair across his face and a somersault legdrop.

Walks to the ring, takes a microphone from the announce table, complains that he is not pushed over 'one name, face painted no talents', says he fought in Pancrase and Pankration, and is attacked by Simon Ezra with a blade.
After the judges name Slater, rolls out for the belt, kisses it, hands it to Slater and raises his hand.

After the Iron Man match and Hansen's gesture, the lights drop, he stands in the ring and double-chokeslams Slater and Hansen, introduces himself as Deathbringer and, in part fifteen, names Casey James, Tiger Claw, Quigley, Annis and others.

matches.stipulation: Television Title triple threat match (Dave Bryant defending)
matches.note: Recapped in part two as held before the broadcast: Bryant defended the Television Title against Sinister and Paragon in a hard-fought triple threat match in which Sinister nearly won several times; Bryant hit Sinister with a chair, tossed it to Paragon, who caught it, and hit the chair into Paragon's face with the Call Me In The Morning, knocking him out cold; a three count later he was still the Television Champion. As Bryant celebrated, Edward Love ran down the aisle and put Paragon through a table (see the Edward Love angle).

matches.stipulation: Tag team match for the number one contendership to the World Tag Team Titles
matches.note: Recapped in part three as held before the broadcast: the Benjamins and the Fracas Boys met with the number one contender spot on the line, and Bobby Benjamin rolled Creed up in a small package to give the Benjamins the win; part four repeats that the Benjamins are the number one contenders. The page names no Benjamin but Bobby, so the side lists him alone.

The opener of the broadcast, in the Tokyo Dome. Tenru hits a boot, a flapjack, a scoop slam, a leg drop, a DDT, a moonsault and the Tenru Special, and gets a Tope Con Hilo, a flying forearm, a Vader Bomb and a springboard legdrop in return; Turk kicks out of the Tenru Special and of a chokeslam and locks on the Turk 911 hold, which Tenru does not tap to when the bell rings. Ken Graham announces a time limit draw and Turk celebrates. After the bell Quinn Brown runs in with a fire extinguisher (see his angle).

Bloodstorm's EMWC debut, in the Tokyo Dome, against the local team of the Tokyo Kid and Fuji. The bell rings as Storm and Vampyro run in; Storm clotheslines Fuji out and Vampyro beats the Kid, hits an asai moonsault, and the pair hit a double powerbomb on the Kid, with Vampyro covering for the three. After the bell Storm tells the crowd 'These are the first'; Vampyro moonsaults the Kid through a table and the House of Lords run in (part two).

matches.stipulation: EMWC North American Title (Mark Langseth defending); one fall
matches.note: Langseth, defending Gabriel Whitecross's title, pokes Myers's eye, works his left leg and drives a chair into it; Myers fights back with an enzugiri, a missile dropkick and a handspring elbow, and lines up the Rattler, but Langseth slams him into a corner, crushing the referee, and uppercuts him in the groin. Serge Annis interrupts over the speakers (see his interference): a dummy dressed as Whitecross on a noose drops from the catwalk and burns, Annis steals Langseth's chains, soaks them in kerosene, sets them on fire and hits Langseth with the Epitomizer on the floor. Langseth is rolled into the ring and Myers, with the referee reviving, hits the Rattler for the three and the title. Chris Blue then orders a triangle match for later that night (part three).

matches.stipulation: Non-title match; one fall, twenty-minute time limit
matches.note: Slater, the World Champion, limps to the ring on a bad knee; Lau comes out with Tiger Claw, six women in nymph costumes, a child who hands him a soft drink and has it spat in his face, and a fan whose shirt reads 'I Love it LAU' and who faints when he kisses her hand. Slater dominates with a knee to the jaw, a piledriver, a spinebuster and a powerbomb until Claw argues with the referee, Lau charges into the referee and Claw's head hits the referee's; Claw pushes Lau out of the Wild Ride spin and knocks Slater cold with a shin kick, and Lau falls on him for the three. Ken Graham gives the time as 4:32; the announcers call it a tainted win.

matches.stipulation: Tag team match; Sam Hell and a mystery partner against the Dead Presidents
matches.note: The Dead Presidents knock Hell to the ground on the ramp before the bell; Sebastian wins the early exchanges, Hell comes back with a drop toe hold, a splash in the corner, a scoop slam and the figure four, and Crash holds the referee's attention while Sebastian taps unseen; after a DDT the Dead Presidents wreck Hell's left knee, Crash dropping it across the ropes and locking on a figure four and Sebastian dropping elbows on it. As the announcers say it may be Hell's last night, 'Fur Elise' plays and Charles Scheffield runs down as the mystery partner; Hell tags him by accident, he clotheslines both Presidents, hits the FieldPlex, and he and Hell win. After the bell Sebastian hits Scheffield, Hell and Hell's knee with a chair; paramedics take Hell out.

matches.stipulation: EMWC Junior Heavyweight Title (Juvenil Infierno defending); one fall
matches.note: Ms. Miki introduces her challenger from Nagoya with Jack Banks looking on; Infierno breathes fire. They trade dropkicks; Infierno hits a piledriver, a 450 splash and a plancha, the Kid a tombstone piledriver on the floor and a shooting star press through the timekeeper's table; Infierno stops the count at nine, misses a no-hands plancha into the guardrail, and the two fight on the top rope until both fall into a small package by Infierno for the three. The announcers say Infierno will defend the title against La Pulga Gigante in Mexico the following week.

matches.stipulation: EMWC World Tag Team Titles (the Down Boys defending); one fall
matches.note: Jinsei Jang, a fan chosen at random as guest ring announcer, is dragged out by security after introducing the Down Boys as the New Age Down Boys; Jivvy goes to the ring with Oliver, Ms. Miki and Jack Banks with the Fabulous Ones. The Down Boys work Sho Satsuma over with a crotch slam, a tilt-a-whirl powerslam, a powerbomb and splash, a brainbuster and a slingshot; Dave Bryant argues with Ms. Miki, storms off, then jumps the guardrail and superkicks Peterson off the top while the referee is arguing with Oliver, and Agito and Sho hit a double stomachbreaker and the Kamikaze Slam for the three. Todd Michaelson announces the Fabulous Ones as the new champions himself.

matches.stipulation: EMWC North American Title (Chris Myers defending); triangle match, one fall, thirty-minute time limit
matches.note: Langseth, bandaged and without his chains, Annis, who comes up through the crowd, and Myers, the champion, who comes last. Annis clotheslines Langseth, power slams him, sets a table and dives through it onto both men, piledrives Myers and hits a double chokeslam on both (Myers gets a shoulder up) and the Epitomizer on Myers; Langseth dropkicks Annis, tackles him over the top rope, and locks the ankle lock on Myers, who passes out. Ken Graham announces Langseth the winner by submission and the new champion.

matches.stipulation: King of the Death Match semifinal; the Killing Box; Texas Death rules (the ten count is started at a competitor's request)
matches.note: A cage of chicken wire, plexiglass, barbed wire mesh and a glass roof, with a board of nails, a board of barbed wire, a board of broken glass and a board of three bombs in the corners; Dick Longfellow referees. Temple smashes Ezra into a bomb in the first minute and throws a chair, a crowbar, a garbage can, a barbed-wire bat and a hangman's noose into the ring, then thumbtacks into Ezra's face; Ezra comes back with a German suplex onto the chair, a crowbar attack, a DDT into the garbage can and a Lygerbomb, and they fight into the crowd and back. Temple climbs onto the glass roof and Ezra follows; Temple piledrives and powerbombs him on the glass, the roof cracks and the Killing Box collapses over both. Longfellow counts ten over the rubble and the bell rings; the page announces no winner, medics dig them out, and both are taken to the hospital. The announcers do not say which man goes on to the final at Devil's Night on 31 October.

matches.stipulation: Triple Cage Tower match; the first man to climb out through the top cage wins and receives a World Title shot at Devil's Night
matches.note: Eight men in a tower of three cages; before the bell Ken Curtis hits Stonebreaker over the head with a chair on the ramp and throws him into the cage. Staley and Quigley trade blows from the start, the Syndicate double-teams Steele, Mota turns on Tiger Claw ('Nothing personal'), Staley takes the Syndi-Cutter and hits a Detonator suplex on Curtis, Quigley reverses Staley's Lethal Injection and applies the Vindicator, and Quigley climbs through to the top cage, where he hits Staley with a fisherman's buster. Tiger Claw climbs up behind him, kicks him off the cage wall, and climbs out through the top to win the shot.

matches.stipulation: WarGames: a double cage of two rings; one man from each team starts, another enters after each interval, and once all eight are inside the match ends only by submission or surrender
matches.note: Quinn Brown starts for Team Spector against Billy Sexton, wearing metal baseball cleats, and cuts Sexton open before Sexton's barbed-wire bat slashes his back; the Body Shop win the coin toss and send in Simon Lebec, who is about to hit Brown with the bat when Joe Reed blocks it and enters. Steve Spector climbs the cage and drops a chair that Ronnie D catches, missile-dropkicks him off the cage, and Trey Porter slams the cage door on Spector's arm before entering. The mystery partner does not appear until Moxy Blue, who had been at the announce table, walks up the ramp; when Ronnie D runs, Moxy pulls his pants down and drags him back, and Team Spector win control. Quinn Brown puts Ronnie D in the Sharpshooter and Ronnie D says 'I quit'. Ken Graham announces Reed, Spector, Brown and Moxy Blue the winners.

matches.stipulation: EMWC World Title (Kevin Slater defending); 60-Minute Iron Man match, the most falls wins
matches.note: The first Iron Man match in the EMWC. Hansen goes after Slater's knee and wins the first fall at 23:29, when referee Dick Longfellow deems Slater unable to answer his questions in the Hangman's Noose; Hansen leads 1-0. Hansen walks out through the curtain, comes back, is dropped by Slater from the ramp into the crowd, and both men are loaded onto stretchers; Slater gets up, pushes Hansen's stretcher into the ring and hits the flying elbow and the Wild Night through a table. Slater wins the second fall at 40:23 with a chair splash after four powerbombs. They trade near falls, a Thunderbomb, a Northern Lights Bomb and a ladder elbow; as the sixty minutes run out Slater splashes Hansen from the top of a ladder through the ramp. Ken Graham announces a tie at one fall each and a draw, but says three judges appointed that day by Chris Blue will decide: judge one Hansen, judge two Slater, the final judge Slater. Slater keeps the title; Hansen kisses the belt and hands it to him.

notes: The EMWC television show An Evening To The Extreme of 30 September 1998 from the Tokyo Dome in Tokyo, Japan, posted on 7 October 1998 in fifteen parts after the operator's note that it was about to be posted, with Jon Stegglet, Todd Michaelson and Richard "Moxy" Blue at the announce table, Ken Graham announcing and Lori Dane reporting. Fourteen matches are worked, two of them recapped from before the broadcast: Dave Bryant keeps the Television Title over Sinister and Paragon; the Benjamins win the number one contendership over the Fracas Boys; Jensei Tenru and Willy Turk go to a time limit draw; Bloodstorm beats the Tokyo Kid and Fuji; Chris Myers beats Mark Langseth for the North American Title; Brian Lau beats Kevin Slater in a non-title match with Tiger Claw's help; Sam Hell and Charles Scheffield beat the Dead Presidents; Juvenil Infierno keeps the Junior Heavyweight Title over Kabuki Kid; the Fabulous Ones win the World Tag Team Titles from the Down Boys; Mark Langseth wins the North American Title back in a triangle match; Simon Ezra and Caleb Temple bring the Killing Box down with no winner announced; Tiger Claw wins the Triple Cage Tower; Quinn Brown, Steve Spector, Joe Reed and Moxy Blue win the WarGames over the Body Shop; and Kevin Slater keeps the World Title over Curtis Hansen in a 60-minute Iron Man match, decided by a split decision of three judges after a tie at one fall each. Parts fourteen and fifteen share seven lines (the end of part fourteen opens part fifteen), and the card's date is the one in the subject line of the note and of part one ('Sept. 30').

name: An Evening To The Extreme

date.source: The subject line of part one, which heads the card 'An Evening To The Extreme (October 7)'; the posts are dated 11 October 1998 and the year is the year of posting; the pages name the Palacio de los Deportes, the Mexican crowd and the Mexico City EMWC faithful.

appearances.note: Walks to the ring to Beck's 'Where It's At', has the music cut, says nobody appreciates what he has done, turns on the retired 'Playboy' Ronnie D, calling him talentless and overrated, promises a new era of shows packed with what the fans want to see, and orders Juvenil Infierno to serve as the lock on the door of the Mexican Death Match.

After the House of Lords' win promises the same match next week in Puerto Rico in a steel cage with Greece banned, and before the Annis and Harris match announces that the winner will meet Caleb Temple and Simon Ezra in the King of the Death Match finals at Devil's Night.
Arrives backstage during the brawl between Chris Quigley and Christopher Stonebreaker and calls Team Extreme off so they can finish it.

Tells Dave Bryant off for mocking Mexican heritage, says Spector will face him that night and Juvenil Infierno the next week, and announces that Quinn Brown will meet Infierno for the Junior Heavyweight Title right away, inside the lowered cage, because La Pulga Gigante is delayed.

After the Television Title match books Trey Porter against Steve Spector in a Strap Match and Dave Bryant against Luke Steele for the Television Title, Falls Count Anywhere in a strip club, both at Devil's Night.

Reads out the Devil's Night line-up so far, is interrupted by the Body Shop, orders Trey Porter to remove the EMWC Universal Championship belt, is Superkicked by Zack Malone into Trey Porter's Heartbreaker and powerbombed through a table by Drago.
At the announce table in a neckbrace, grimacing in pain, with Jon Stegglet and Todd Michaelson, who josh him about his neck.

Comes to the ring as the special referee of the Mexican Death Match after Chris Blue overrules his representatives' refusal, is distracted at the cage door by Hakiro Matsuoko, starts the ten count on the fallen men, and rings the bell when Tenru's feet touch the floor.
Hits Dave Bryant with a Tilt-a-Whirl Powerbomb and a hurricanrana from the top after Chris Blue's dressing-down, until Glory and Elena pull Bryant clear to the floor.

During the Mexican Death Match flies to ringside, climbs the cage and hits Jensei Tenru with a missile dropkick and a Ligerbomb, then climbs out and stays at ringside; Todd Michaelson calls it unfair and Moxy Blue says he was evening the odds.

In new black wrestling pants with red trim and white face paint with a black eagle, takes the microphone after the match and asks Quinn Brown for his answer on the Daimyo; accepts Brown's refusal with a bow and says the Daimyo will be there should Brown ever change his mind.
Tosses a chair over the top of the cage to Jensei Tenru, slides a rattan cane and the house microphone into the ring, and moves to enter the cage, which draws Juvenil Infierno to the door.

After the Mexican Death Match takes the microphone from Kabuki Kid: Thunder and Lightning lives but there is no Daimyo, he will not live under the same banner as Dave Bryant, and he challenges Bryant directly while offering his hand to the Daimyo as an ally.
Comes out of a locker room with the Benjamins to separate Chris Quigley and Christopher Stonebreaker backstage.
With Zombie and Gothic Mary in a taped scene in the parking lot, joins a gathering of the Vogon Poet's Guild before the show.
In a taped scene in the parking lot, steps to a microphone in front of the Vogon Poet's Guild and recites a chant about Logan and Style, 'Destroyed by us'.
Appears in the aisleway with the House of Lords before their match against Anarchy, to catcalls from the crowd.

Walks out through a ring of fire to an 'Anus stinks!' chant carrying a glass pane in a black wrapper; tells Casey James to back off, tells Mark Langseth he owes him his title or his soul, welcomes Gabriel Whitecross back, tells Chris Myers of the Cult of Personality that he is no match for Annis, and announces the Seven Pains of Glass stipulation for his match against Matt Harris.
Stands bandaged in the middle of the ring when the lights come back, with Gabriel Whitecross, Chris Myers and Mark Langseth, as the broadcast runs out of time.

Interviewed in the ring by Jon Stegglet to 'For Those About to Rock'; says nothing went wrong in the Triple Cage Tower match, belittles each contender he names, mentions Deathbringer and Halloween, and slaps the microphone out of Stegglet's hand.

Is jumped backstage by Ken Curtis, fights back with a chair, a garbage-can DDT and a refreshment table, hits Curtis in the chest with Christopher Stonebreaker's sledgehammer, and brawls with Stonebreaker with a mop bucket and a steel pipe until a locker room empties.

Does not come to the ring for his scheduled match against Chris Quigley: shown backstage kicking a fallen Quigley and hurling him into a garage door, is hit with a chair and thrown into a refreshment table, fights Christopher Stonebreaker, is hit in the face and chest with a sledgehammer by Quigley, and leaves for the hospital.
