Swings a sledgehammer at Ken Curtis backstage and misses, fights him, and then brawls with Chris Quigley, choking Quigley with a broom handle until Quigley drills him with a mop bucket and chokes him with a steel pipe; gets soap in Quigley's eyes, hurls him into a wall and smashes a hole in it with the sledgehammer.
Is shown in the upper deck staring coldly at Chris Quigley as Quigley leaves the arena after his interview.

Meets Lori Dane outside the Cult of Personality's locker room before his main event with Gabriel Whitecross, with sunken, bloodshot eyes; says he looks forward to a good, solid match and that anything can happen.
Walks to the ring slowly, with depression on his face, and sits in the corner for the main event against Gabriel Whitecross, which does not start before the broadcast runs out of time.
Returns to the EMWC to 'Something Wicked' and rolls into the ring for the main event against Chris Myers, which the broadcast runs out of time to show.

As North American Champion comes down the aisle to boos and takes the microphone: 'You boys were ready to party without me? Let's make this song a trio!', as the lights go out and Serge Annis appears in the ring.

Walks out with a stitched-up face carrying a razor-wire bat and a barbed-wire chair and screams a promo at Simon Ezra, the Blood Angel, beating the ring with the bat, swinging the chair at air and pulling out his own stitches.

Comes to the ring behind Matt Harris holding the gold-plated cheese grater and carrying the black duffel bag, tosses chairs, canes, bats, garbage cans and the grater into the ring during the match, and helps Harris pull a pane of glass out of its frame.

Comes out in a mask with Elena and Glory, takes it off in the ring after losing a mask-versus-bra match, mocks the Mexican crowd with 'Orale!' and 'Arriba la raza!', and begins a promo about Steve Spector.

Continues his promo, naming Jak Martin and Marcus Renge as former World Heavyweight Champions he beat; is interrupted and told off by Chris Blue, and hit with a Tilt-a-Whirl Powerbomb by Juvenil Infierno.
After keeping the title, calls Luke Steele on, trades blows with him on the apron and is hit with an ocean cyclone suplex before security breaks it up.
With Elena, comes to the ring with the masked Dave Bryant; later pulls Bryant clear of Juvenil Infierno.
With Glory, comes to the ring with the masked Dave Bryant; later pulls Bryant clear of Juvenil Infierno.
After losing the Television Title match, is whipped by Trey Porter with a leather strap until Team Extreme subdues the men; Chris Blue books the Strap Match.

Walks out during the Television Title match with a leather strap and shouts up at Steve Spector on the top rope, a distraction that lets Dave Bryant recover and win; after the bell slides in and whips Spector with the strap.

With Zack Malone and Drago, claims the EMWC Universal Championship, takes the microphone to say Ronnie D is at home because 'DTP decided it so', tells Steve Spector what to expect on the other end of the leather strap at Devil's Night, and hits Chris Blue with the Heartbreaker after Malone's Superkick.
Comes to ringside to 'I Am The Man' in a 'Props to the CoP' T-shirt and joins Jon Stegglet and Moxy Blue on commentary for the Television Title match.
Leaves the booth when Dave Bryant calls him on after the match, trades blows with Bryant on the apron and hits an ocean cyclone suplex before security breaks it up.
With Tiger Claw, searches the building for Serge Annis, forces Annis's dressing-room door and finds it empty, then learns that the Syndicate's dressing room is on fire.
With Casey James, searches the halls for Serge Annis and kicks in his dressing-room door, then watches the Syndicate's burning dressing room with a slight grin.

Walks out unannounced in jeans and a T-shirt and gives a bitter speech listing his ten months in the EMWC and the stars who get more attention, begs for one last chance against anyone, and leaps with a legdrop through the announce table.

As World Tag Team Champion with Sho Satsuma, comes to the ring with Ms. Miki and Jack Banks, warns the Benjamins that the Fabulous Ones will be ready for their title match at the next pay-per-view, and poses for the crowd.
With Agito Nakajima, tells the Benjamins that the Fabulous Ones will stay the tag champions, and takes his shirt off for the crowd.
Introduces the Fabulous Ones as the world tag team champions and takes the belt from Agito Nakajima.
Comes to the ring with Ms. Miki and the Fabulous Ones and stays at ringside.

Walks out with Billy Sexton in a '#1 Free Agent' T-shirt, turns down the requests to replace Ronnie D in the Snake Den, challenges Trey Porter to a Halloween Blood Match at the pay-per-view with no rules, and leaves with Sexton.
Comes to the ring with Simon Lebec, hands him the bat, and leaves with him.
Comes to the ring with Tiger Claw; while Claw occupies the referee, karate chops Joe Reed, who hits him with a chair; Lau is out of action for a time.
Gets into the ring after Claw's win, points to Claw as the man to beat and applauds with a hearty, evil laugh.
Comes to the ring to 'Sexual Thing' in a ZMWC T-shirt with Cheryl Amber and Trey Porter and Drago, says he and Porter built the Body Shop, and Superkicks Chris Blue in the head.
Follows Zack Malone through the curtain.
Follows Trey Porter to the ring, knocks a fan in a 'FREE RONNIE' shirt down with a forearm, and powerbombs Chris Blue through a table at ringside.

Appears on a tape shown on Chris Blue's orders from a bar in Cabo Wabo, Mexico: retired, with a championship belt, he claims 163 straight humiliations of Chris Quigley and asks the fans to show him a sign they want him back.

matches.stipulation: Mexican Death Match; a steel cage; the only way to win is to throw the opponent over the top of the cage to the floor; Juvenil Infierno is the special referee
matches.note: The opener of the broadcast. Hakiro Matsuoko walks Tenru to the ring and Brown climbs one of the ropes that lower the cage, and drops onto Tenru from the top with a clothesline. Brown hits a satellite head scissors, a rana and an inside Asai moonsault press in baseball spikes that open Tenru up; Tenru answers with a powerslam, a DDT, a brainbuster, a chair tossed over the cage by Matsuoko, a guillotine legdrop across a chair, a triple jump moonsault, the Nodowa Bomb and a moonsault from the top of the cage. With Infierno distracted by Matsuoko, Kabuki Kid climbs the cage and hits Tenru with a missile dropkick and a Ligerbomb. Infierno counts to nine over the two men before both rise; Brown hits an 810 splash, takes Tenru up the cage, and kicks him in the face until Tenru, hanging by one arm, falls through the Spanish announce table; Tenru's feet touch the floor, Infierno rings the bell and Ken Graham announces Brown.

matches.stipulation: Tag team match; one fall
matches.note: The House of Lords, with their manager, return to the EMWC against Anarchy, introduced by a woman in a tight dress who calls herself Ms. Miki; the bell is a large ringside bell. Style and Zombie start; Anarchy's boots, a bulldog on the cement and a hammerlock weblock are traded until the fans of the Vogon Poet's Guild drag Logan into the crowd with a chain and Anarchy dropkicks Style over the barricade; Zombie tickles the referee at nine to restart the count-out; Anarchy then removes the barricade and the Guild fills the ring and the ringside; a Guild member hits Style with a chair; Logan rolls in behind a laughing MadDog and hits the heart punch for the three. The fans from Greece then charge in, Team Extreme breaks up the riot, and Chris Blue promises the same match next week in Puerto Rico in a steel cage with Greece banned.

matches.stipulation: King of the Death Match semifinal; Seven Pains of Glass Death Match; seven panes of glass on platforms around the ring; to win, put the opponent through four of them
matches.note: Annis announces the stipulation in the ring; Matt Harris comes down with Sydney and the gold-plated cheese grater. Harris clotheslines Annis onto a platform, powerbombs him through the first pane, grates his forehead with the grater, pulls a pane out of its frame and breaks it over Annis's head for two, and puts him through a third with the Harris Special. Annis counters with the Epitomizer, piles four panes on the floor and powerbombs Harris through all four. Ken Graham announces Annis, who goes to the finals at Devil's Night against Caleb Temple and Simon Ezra.

matches.stipulation: EMWC Junior Heavyweight Title (Juvenil Infierno defending); steel cage; one fall, the first man out over the top wins
matches.note: La Pulga Gigante is delayed by travel; Chris Blue announces Quinn Brown as the challenger and lowers the cage, though Brown has already wrestled that night. They trade an Asai moonsault, a hurricanrana, baseball-spike dropkicks that cut Infierno's mask, a superkick, an enzuigiri, a spinning leg lariat, a sitting powerbomb and a somersault legdrop; Infierno hits a springboard German release suplex off the side of the cage; Brown climbs after him, stops him going over, and is slammed face-first into the steel; Infierno's frog splash from the top of the cage knocks the wind out of both men. Dick Longfellow unlocks the cage, calls the medical crew and the broadcast cuts away with neither man moving; no result is announced. Chris Blue later announces Brown against Infierno inside a steel cage at Devil's Night.

matches.stipulation: EMWC Television Title (Dave Bryant defending); one fall
matches.note: Bryant comes out in a mask, loses it in the ring and cuts a promo; Spector wrestles through an injured arm. Luke Steele joins the announce table and trades remarks with Moxy Blue; Bryant works the arm with hammerlocks and a facelock, a moonsault through the timekeeper's table and a springboard legdrop onto the arm. Spector hits a flying DDT, flying headscissors and a flying legdrop. Trey Porter walks out with a leather strap and shouts up at Spector on the top rope; Bryant climbs up and hits the Ultimate Prescription from the second turnbuckle for the three. After the bell Porter whips Spector with the strap, Bryant attacks Steele and Steele hits an ocean cyclone suplex, and Team Extreme breaks it up.

matches.stipulation: One fall
matches.note: Brian Lau walks Claw out; Reed takes the early advantage with a hiptoss, a double stomp, a spinebuster and a reverse anklelock. Claw thrusts to the groin, Lau karate chops Reed, and Reed goes outside and hits Lau with a chair. Reed rolls Claw up and powerbombs him; Claw kicks out of each cover, hits a step-up enzuigiri, the Claw Driver and a knee drop from the top, the Golden Tiger Strike, for the three. Chris Blue's line-up has Claw facing the World Champion Kevin Slater in a Towel Match at Devil's Night.

notes: The EMWC television show An Evening To The Extreme of 7 October 1998 from the Palacio de los Deportes in Mexico City, posted on 11 October 1998 in six parts, with Jon Stegglet, Todd Michaelson and Richard "Moxy" Blue at the announce table, Ken Graham announcing and Lori Dane reporting. Six matches are recorded, one of them an unfinished cage match: Quinn Brown wins the Mexican Death Match over Jensei Tenru; the House of Lords beat Anarchy; Serge Annis beats Matt Harris in the Seven Pains of Glass match and goes to the King of the Death Match finals; Juvenil Infierno and Quinn Brown are left lying in the cage with no result announced; Dave Bryant keeps the Television Title over Steve Spector; Tiger Claw beats Joe Reed. Ken Curtis and Chris Quigley are scheduled to fight but brawl backstage with Christopher Stonebreaker instead, and the main event of Gabriel Whitecross against Chris Myers is not shown before the broadcast runs out of time. The card is the one after the Tokyo Dome show of 30 September, which the announcers call last week.
